video.title: Board of Trustees of the Affordable Housing Trust (AHT) 3/25/26

summary.body: Board of Trustees of the Affordable Housing Trust
summary.headline: The Affordable Housing Trust reorganized leadership, discussed a proposed 60-unit Southville Road project, and considered acquiring land on Northborough Road.
summary.summary: The Affordable Housing Trust elected Paul Desmond as chair and Ellen Marya as vice chair to establish a rotating leadership model. Developer James Venincasa presented details on a proposed 60-unit MBTA Communities multifamily development on Southville Road and discussed the feasibility of town subsidies for additional affordability. The board also reviewed the Community Preservation Committee's approval of its funding application for Annual Town Meeting and evaluated the potential acquisition of a 1.47-acre parcel on Northborough Road for affordable housing.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board reviewed and approved past meeting minutes and voted to release executive session minutes.
key_details: Approved regular meeting minutes from January 20, 2026, as amended.
Approved and voted to release executive session minutes from February 18, 2026, concerning 150 Framingham Road following the sale of that property.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved and executive minutes released.

topics.title: Southville Road apartment complex proposal
topics.summary: Developer James Venincasa met with the trust to review a 60-unit residential proposal on a 4-acre site on Southville Road within the MBTA Communities zoning district. The board explored whether municipal funds could buy down additional affordable units beyond the mandated 10 percent, though the developer noted that 30-year amortized rent reductions create substantial financing gaps that often require millions of dollars in subsidies.
key_details: Project site is 4 acres on Southville Road, zoned under MBTA Communities for up to 15 units per acre.
Current proposal features 60 units across two 3-story buildings (roughly 2.5 stories design) with an optional clubhouse.
Under MBTA zoning, 10 percent of units (6 units) will be designated affordable.
Development costs are tracking between the high $300,000s and $500,000 per unit, with land acquisition near $2,000,000.
The developer agreed to estimate the dollar figure required if the town sought to subsidize an additional affordable unit.
topics.outcome: Developer will provide estimated cost projections for adding an affordable unit.
topics.why_it_matters: The project represents a major multifamily development in town, and municipal subsidies could affect how many units are permanently affordable to low- and moderate-income residents.

topics.title: Election of chair and vice chair
topics.summary: Outgoing chair Doug announced his intention to step down from the role to encourage rotating leadership among members. Paul Desmond was nominated and elected as the new chair, and Ellen Marya was elected vice chair.
key_details: Doug served as chair for roughly a year and advocated for rotating leadership to distribute administrative duties.
Paul Desmond accepted nomination and was elected chair.
Ellen Marya accepted nomination and was elected vice chair.
topics.outcome: Paul Desmond elected chair and Ellen Marya elected vice chair.

topics.title: Community Preservation Committee application and Town Meeting preparations
topics.summary: Ellen Marya reported that the Community Preservation Committee voted to recommend the Affordable Housing Trust's funding application for the Annual Town Meeting warrant. The board discussed presentation logistics, opting for a brief presentation and an informational one-page handout for voters.
key_details: The CPC approved the Trust's application with one dissenting vote.
The CPC application leaves roughly $100,000 in unallocated housing funds with the CPC.
Annual Town Meeting is scheduled for Saturday, April 11, 2026.
Doug and Ellen Marya will coordinate on a short slide presentation and a one-page informational summary handout.
topics.outcome: Application advances to Town Meeting; members will prepare presentation materials.
topics.why_it_matters: Annual Town Meeting approval of Community Preservation Act funds directly provides the capital needed for the Trust to finance affordable housing efforts.

topics.title: 55+ housing bylaw update and zoning initiatives
topics.summary: The board received an update that the proposed 55+ housing bylaw will be targeted for Fall Town Meeting rather than Spring Town Meeting. Members also discussed coordinating with the Planning Board on wider zoning opportunities, such as Chapter 40Y starter-home zoning.
key_details: Action on the 55+ housing bylaw was postponed to the Fall Town Meeting to allow further joint work with the Planning Board.
Board members discussed starter-home zoning models (Chapter 40Y) that permit smaller single-family lots with lower frontage requirements.
topics.outcome: Discussion to resume after Spring Town Meeting.

topics.title: Northborough Road parcel evaluation
topics.summary: The board evaluated a 1.47-acre parcel on Northborough Road subject to a Chapter 61A right of first refusal at a price of $216,000. Members debated the parcel's development viability, noting that while the front portion has favorable soils for septic, the rear contains wetlands and requires quick action if the town wants to exercise its option.
key_details: Parcel size is 1.47 acres on Northborough Road with a fixed purchase price of $216,000.
Town must decide whether to exercise its Chapter 61A right of first refusal within a 120-day statutory window.
Front half of the parcel appears suitable for on-site septic based on soil maps, while the rear is wetland.
A non-profit housing developer advised a board member that small projects of 6 to 9 units struggle with subsidy thresholds, whereas a duplex or partnership with Habitat for Humanity could be viable.
Member Al Hamilton offered to check percolation test records with the Board of Health and contact Habitat for Humanity for site review.
topics.outcome: Members will investigate site percolation records and developer interest before taking formal action.
topics.why_it_matters: Exercising the town's statutory right to purchase this land could secure town-owned property for affordable housing development at a relatively low land cost.

topics.title: Technical assistance grant application
topics.summary: Ellen Marya noted that the Massachusetts Housing Partnership Mini-Boost technical assistance grant application remains open. The grant could fund consultant support for community engagement and strategic planning for the Trust.
key_details: MHP Mini-Boost grant offers technical assistance funding for defined municipal housing planning projects.
Ellen Marya will circulate the application materials to the board for review.
topics.outcome: Application materials to be circulated for discussion at the next meeting.

votes.motion: Elect Paul Desmond as Chair of the Affordable Housing Trust.
Elect Ellen Marya as Vice Chair of the Affordable Housing Trust.
Enter into executive session under M.G.L. Chapter 30A, Section 21(a)(6) to consider the purchase, exchange, lease or value of real property, not to return to open session.
